title: Best Women's Leggings UK
short: Running, gym, maternity and everyday leggings compared by fit, fabric, pockets and price, from budget to premium.
intro: Good leggings should stay put, not go see-through when you squat, and suit whatever you're doing in them. This guide compares leggings tested by Women's Running and Marie Claire UK, spanning running, the gym, maternity wear and everyday styling, from budget high-street picks to premium technical pairs.

guide.q: What should I look for in gym vs running leggings?
guide.a: Gym leggings need to be squat-proof (not see-through when stretched) with strong four-way stretch. Running leggings benefit more from moisture-wicking fabric, a secure waistband and sometimes a UPF rating for sun protection.

guide.q: How do I know if leggings will go see-through?
guide.a: Reviewers stretch the fabric or bend over in a mirror before buying. Thicker, squat-proof fabrics and darker colours are less likely to show through, and Women's Running notes lighter colours can show marks and sweat more easily.

guide.q: Do I need pockets in running leggings?
guide.a: If you run with a phone, keys or gels, pockets save carrying a belt or bag. Thigh pockets suit phones, while smaller waist pockets suit cards and keys.

Premium leggings often last much longer, as the Sweaty Betty Zero Gravity example shows after 8 years of wear, which can make the cost per wear lower over time. Budget options like the M&S Goodmove range can still perform well for occasional use.

guide.q: What should I look for in maternity leggings?
guide.a: A good maternity legging needs enough stretch to grow with you from early pregnancy to full term without digging in, plus a supportive over-bump or under-bump panel. Seamless styles, like the Seraphine Ultimate here, tend to be the most versatile, working for both light workouts and everyday lounging or postpartum wear.
